claims.text: Dispersed nanoscale oxide reinforcements will improve the high-temperature mechanical performance of refractory high-entropy alloys.
Oxide-reinforced refractory high-entropy alloys will retain irradiation stability.
Oxide-reinforced refractory high-entropy alloys will retain thermal stability.
Y2O3 nanoparticles can serve as thermally stable oxide reinforcements in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Uniformly dispersed oxide nanoparticles act as barriers to dislocation motion.
Uniformly dispersed oxide nanoparticles act as sinks for irradiation-induced defects.
The nanoparticle dispersion increases resistance to creep.
The nanoparticle dispersion increases resistance to radiation damage.
Oxide nanoparticles provide energetically favorable sites for recombination of irradiation-induced defects.
Defect recombination at oxide nanoparticles mitigates defect-cluster formation under irradiation.
The modified alloy will have greater high-temperature tensile strength than an otherwise comparable alloy without oxide nanoparticles.
The modified alloy will have greater high-temperature creep strength than an otherwise comparable alloy without oxide nanoparticles.
The modified alloy will undergo less irradiation-induced degradation than an otherwise comparable alloy without oxide nanoparticles.
The beneficial effects require a controlled, fine, and uniform nanoparticle dispersion.
Excessive nanoparticle content or agglomeration can create weak interfaces and reduce overall performance.
The intervention is limited to alloy compositions that are compatible with the selected oxide.
